notes:
Account summary: Tradewind Aurora is a mid-market analytics SaaS (customer-facing support + search) evaluating Redwood for inference consolidation. They started on Hosted API to validate capabilities; now moving to a Dedicated POC to hit cost and latency targets.

Key stakeholders: CTO Evan Park (platform), Eng Lead Maria Torres (ML infra), Head of Product Jonas Reed, Procurement: Dana Liu. AE: Priya Nair; SE: Marcus Lee.

Use-case details / requirements (direct from calls):
- Primary: support-agent (real-time chat for customer support) + doc-search and reranking for knowledge base retrieval.
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for short chat turns (<60 tokens) — "'critical for end-user experience'" (Maria).
- Throughput target: baseline 120 req/s; peak expected 180 req/s during batch re-ranks.
- Cost sensitivity: finance target is ~30-50% reduction vs current Hosted per-token spend after moving to Dedicated and quantization.
- Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified models; willing to test quantized variants. Plan to compare rw-gptx-8k-q4 (dedicated) vs rw-gptx-8k-pt (hosted baseline).
- Routing/fallback needs: must support region failover (us-east -> us-west) and fallback to Hosted API if Dedicated pool exhausted. Canary routing required for safe rollouts.

POC scope (agreed):
- Duration: 4 weeks.
- Goals: validate latency SLOs, confirm 30-50% cost reduction on typical workload, prove automatic fallback and rollback behavior without customer-visible errors.
- Tests: synthetic load (ramp to 2x expected peak), real query replay from anonymized production traces, quality checks vs labelled eval set (support_kb_eval_v1).

Canary + routing plan (technical outline for POC):
- Phase 0 (smoke): deploy Dedicated pool (2 x A100-equivalent) in us-east, baseline small internal test.
- Phase 1 (canary 5%): route 5% of production-like traffic to Dedicated; warm KV and prefix caches for 48h; monitor error rate, p95 latency, and semantic similarity on eval set.
- Phase 2 (ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 24-48h windows if metrics stable.
- Fallback policy: if Dedicated reports capacity errors or p95 > 500ms or error rate > 2% sustained for 5m, traffic automatically shifts to Hosted API variant with same model family.
- Region failover: secondary Dedicated pool in us-west as standby; route to us-west when us-east AZ shows degraded network or capacity. Failover via smart routing policy; DNS TTLs and session stickiness considered.
- Model variants: primary rw-gptx-8k-q4 (quantized) on Dedicated; fallback rw-gptx-8k-pt (hosted full-precision) and a smaller rw-gptx-4k-qa for low-cost reranks.
- Rollback triggers: quality regression > 3% drop on eval metric, error spike > 2% above baseline, or cost > estimated target by >20% for sustained 24h.

Metrics / success criteria for POC:
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for chat; p50 < 80ms.
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/s with <1% throttling.
- Quality: cosine similarity / semantic match scores within 1-2% of hosted baseline on support_kb_eval_v1.
- Cost: per-1M-token cost reduced by target range (30-50%) including infra and Tail SLO buffer.
- Reliability: zero customer-visible errors during rollouts; automated fallback validated.

Pricing conversation notes: procurement wants a 12-month reserved commitment discount for Dedicated. Finance needs a modeled TCO including model variant licensing and expected token volumes. AE sent preliminary estimate 2026-02-24; procurement requested a revised deck with line items.

Security & compliance notes: Tradewind requires SSO/SAML integration and KMS-based key management for model logs. They asked for retention controls and audit logging for all inference requests. Security team requested SOC2 type II report and pen-test summary before contract.

Current blockers: internal capex approval for reserved GPUs (Procurement), final KMS integration diagram for security, and confirmation of regional SLA for failover.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-12: SE-run test harness handoff & POC runbook (Marcus).
- 2026-03-15: Kickoff — deploy Dedicated dev pool and start Phase 0 smoke tests.
- 2026-03-22: First canary snapshot and quality check vs support_kb_eval_v1.
